questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an instrument of the monetary policy of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goods and Services Tax (GST)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** is NOT an instrument of **the monetary policy of the Reserve Bank of India**.
 
• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a tax on goods and services. It is an indirect tax that was implemented to replace a variety of other indirect taxes such as **VAT, service tax, purchase tax, excise duty,** and so on.
 
• GST is a tax applied in India on the supply of certain goods and services. It is a single tax that applies throughout India.
 
• The fundamental goal of this taxing scheme, which is applicable throughout India, is to reduce the cascading effect of other indirect taxes.
 
• **India **implemented the Goods and Services Tax on **July 1, 2017**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) **uses a liquidity adjustment facility (LAF) to allow banks to borrow money through repurchase agreements (repos) or make loans to the RBI through reverse repo agreements.
 
• **The cash reserve ratio (CRR)** is the amount of liquid cash a bank must keep as a percentage of total deposits.
 
• **The repo rate** is the rate at which a country's central bank (in India, the Reserve Bank of India) loans money to commercial banks in the event of a cash shortage.

questions.question: Which tissue among the following is a protective tissue in the animal body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Epithelial tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Epithelial tissue is a** protective tissue** in the animal body.
 
• **Epithelial tissue** is one of the **four primary forms of bodily tissue** that may be found in human organs and covers both internal and external surfaces.
 
• Depending on where it resides in the human body, it has a variety of structures and functions.
 
• The epithelium is a type of body tissue that covers all of your internal and external body surfaces, lines body cavities and hollow organs, and is the main tissue in glands.
 
• **Protection, secretion, and absorption **are all roles of epithelial tissue, depending on where it's positioned in the human body.
 
• Epithelial cells make up epithelial tissue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Muscle tissue **is made up of cells with the unique capacity to shorten or contract in order to move the body's parts.
 
• The brain, spinal cord, and nerves all include** nerve tissue.** It is in charge of coordinating and controlling various bodily functions.
 
• **Connective tissue** also stores fat, aids in the transportation of nutrients and other substances between tissues and organs, and aids in the repair of damaged tissue.

questions.question: Which law was imposed in India during the command of General Dyer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Martial law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Martial law** was imposed in India during the **command of General Dyer.** 
 
• **On April 13, 1919, General Dyer** signed the Martial Law Act, which stated that no more than two people might establish a group and congregate in one location.
 
• This law was passed to prohibit any organised opposition to the reigning powers.
 
• This occurred during the Sikh festival of Baisakhi when hundreds had congregated in** Jallianwala Bagh to celebrate, and General Dyer** opened fire on them.
 
• **Except for Article 34**, which gives Parliament the ability to reimburse persons for crimes committed in regions where martial law was in effect and to recognise acts committed under martial law, there is no explicit mention of "martial law" in the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Penal Code, 1860 (Section 153 A): **Use of language that promotes discrimination or violence against people on the grounds of race, caste, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other category is illegal.
 
• **Preventive detention** is the practice of incarcerating accused individuals before trial on the idea that their release would be detrimental to society—specifically, that they would be more likely to commit new crimes if released.

questions.question: Which among the following is a Harappan city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dholavira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dholavira** is an archaeological site in **Khadirbet, Bhachau Taluka, Kutch District, Gujarat**, named after a modern-day town 1 kilometre south of it. Radhanpur is 165 kilometres away from this settlement.
 
• The site, also known locally as Kotada timba, features the ruins of an old** Indus Valley Civilization settlement**.
 
• **The Tropic of Cancer** runs through Dholavira. It is one of the five major Harappan sites in India and one of the most important Indus Valley Civilization archaeological sites.
 
• It is also thought to have been the most magnificent city of its period.
 
• It's on Khadir Bet Island in the Great Rann of Kutch's Kutch Desert Wildlife Sanctuary.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Indus Valley Civilisation**, also known as the Harappan Civilisation or the Indus Civilisation, was a Bronze Age civilisation in northwestern South Asia that lasted from 3300 BCE to 1300 BCE, and from 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE in its mature form.
 
• It thrived in the Indus River basins, which flows through the length of Pakistan, and along a system of perennial, largely monsoon-fed rivers that originally ran across northwest India and eastern Pakistan near the seasonal Ghaggar-Hakra river.
 
• **Lumbini** is a Buddhist pilgrimage place in Nepal's Lumbini Province's Rupandehi District. 
 
• **The Empire of Kosala **was an ancient Indian kingdom with a rich culture that spanned the territory from modern-day Uttar Pradesh to Western Odisha.
 
• **Hampi** is a historic village in Karnataka, India's southernmost state. Numerous damaged temple complexes from the Vijayanagara Empire dot the landscape.

questions.question: Whitewashed walls appear to be shiny after three to four days due to the formation of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**calcium carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Whitewashed **walls appear to be shiny after three to four days due to the** formation of calcium carbonate**.
 
• The whitewash contains calcium hydroxide. It forms a thin layer of calcium carbonate on the walls by slowly reacting with carbon dioxide in the air.
 
• After three to four days of whitewashing, calcium carbonate is created.
 
• As a result, after three to four days, the walls have a shiny white finish.
 
• **Ca(OH)₂₍ₐq₎ + CO₂₍g₎ → CaCO₃₍ₛ₎ + H₂O₍ₗ₎**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The chemical compound** calcium carbonate has the formula CaCO₃.** It is the major component of eggshells, gastropod shells, shellfish skeletons, and pearls and is found in rocks such as the minerals calcite and aragonite.
 
• **Calcium nitrate,** is an inorganic chemical with the formula Ca(NO₃)₂ₓ.
 
• **Calcium sulphate** and its hydrates are inorganic compounds with the formula CaSO₄.
 
• **Calcium oxide**, often known as lime or more particularly quicklime, is a white or greyish white solid made by burning calcium carbonate to remove carbon dioxide.

questions.question: The onus of Jallianwala Bagh massacre that happened in 1919 was on which General of the British Army?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**General Dyer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The onus of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre **that happened in **1919 was on General Dyer of the British Army.**
 
• On April 13, 1919, the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, also known as the Amritsar massacre, occurred.
 
• The arrest of pro-Indian independence leaders Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satya Pal drew a largely peaceful crowd to the Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, Punjab.
 
• The temporary Brigadier general R. E. H. Dyer surrounded the demonstrators with his Gurkha British Indian army unit, Sindh Sikh regiment, and 52nd Sikh regiment in response to the public gathering.
 
• The attack was denounced by Secretary of State for War Winston Churchill as "unutterably horrible," and members of Parliament voted 247 to 37 against Dyer in a House of Commons debate on July 8, 1920.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Colonel Reginald Edward Harry Dyer** was a Bengal Army officer who eventually joined the newly formed British Indian Army. Because of his order to fire on a peaceful crowd, he has been dubbed "the Butcher of Amritsar."
 
• **Horatio Herbert Kitchener** was an Anglo-Irish colonial administrator and senior British Army officer.
 
• The first British Governor of the Bengal Presidency was **Major-General Robert Clive,** 1st Baron Clive, commonly known as Clive of India. 
 
• **Major-General Stringer Lawrence,** the first Commander-in-Chief of Fort William, was an English soldier.

questions.question: Who among the following is a famous Santoor player?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandit Shivkumar Sharma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Shivkumar Sharma **was a santoor player and Indian classical musician who is credited for modifying the instrument for Indian classical music.
 
• He worked as a music composer alongside Indian flautist Hariprasad Chaurasia under the moniker Shiv–Hari, and composed music for a number of Indian films.
 
• In 1986, Sharma received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, in 1991, the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian award, and in 2001, the Padma Bhushan, India's third-highest civilian award.
 
• **The Santoor **Instrument is a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer made of walnut that is popular in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Zakir Hussain Allaraka Qureshi **was born in Bombay, India, on March 9, 1951. He is the son of renowned Indian tabla player Ustad Allah Rakha Khan.
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar** was an Indian musician and composer best known for popularising the Sitar, an Indian classical instrument.
 
• **Bismillah Khan,** often known as Ustad, was an Indian musician who is credited with popularising the reeded woodwind instrument Shehnai.

questions.question: Which city bagged the first rank as the cleanest city of India under Swachh Survekshan League 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indore** was named **India's Cleanest City for the fifth yea**r in a row by **Swachh Survekshan**, with** Surat and Vijayawada taking second and third place** in the more than 1 lakh people category, respectively.
 
• Vita, Lonavala, and Sasvad, all in Maharashtra, took first, second, and third place in the population category of "less than 1 lakh" accordingly.
 
• **Varanasi **was named** 'Best Ganga Town,' **and** Ahmedabad Cantonment** was named 'India's Cleanest Cantonment,' ahead of Meerut Cantonment and Delhi Cantonment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**(MoHUA) has released the** Swachh Survekshan 2020** report.
 
• The annual cleanliness urban study undertaken by the MoHUA is in its fifth year.
 
• It is one of the largest sanitation surveys in the world. **Swachh Survekshan** is a ranking exercise undertaken by the Indian government to analyze the cleanliness of rural and urban areas, as well as the prompt and inventive execution of Swachhata's mission efforts.
 
• The survey's goal is to stimulate widespread public participation and raise awareness among all segments of society about the significance of working together to make cities and towns more livable.

questions.question: The 15th Finance Commission has been constituted by the President of India for a period of ______ years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The 15th Finance commission **was established to make recommendations for a** five-year period beginning on April 1, 2020**.
 
• The commission's major goals were to **"strengthen cooperative federalism, increase the quality of government spending, and contribute to fiscal stability."**
 
• The Government of India established the Fifteenth Finance Commission in November 2017 after receiving assent from the President of India through a notification in the Indian Gazette.
 
• The commission's chairman is **Nand Kishore Singh**, and its full-time members are** Shaktikanta Das **and **Anoop Singh**, with part-time members Ramesh Chand and Ashok Lahiri.
 
• Shaktikanta Das, who resigned from the commission to become the governor of the Reserve Bank of India, was replaced by **Ajay Narayan Jha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

 
• **The Finance Commissions** are commissions appointed by the President of India on a regular basis under **Article 280 of the Indian Constitution** to define the financial connections between the central government and state governments.
 
• The** Finance Commission Act of 1951** constituted the** First Commission 1951**.
 
• The most current Finance Commission, chaired by** N. K. Singh,** a former member of the Planning Commission, was established in 2017.
 
• The Commission is appointed every five years, according to the Constitution, and consists of a chairperson and four additional members.

questions.question: The book ‘Gitanjali’ is authored by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabindranath Tagore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gitanjali** is a collection of poems by **Rabindranath Tagore**, a Bengali poet.
 
• Tagore was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Literature, **largely for Song Offerings, his English translation.
 
• It is part of the **UNESCO Representative Works Collection**. On August 14, 1910, the original Bengali collection of 156/157 poems was published.
 
• Rabindranath Tagore was a poet, novelist, playwright, composer, philosopher, social reformer, and painter from Bengal.
 
• With Contextual Modernism in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, he altered Bengali literature and music, as well as Indian art.
 
• He was the **first non-European** and the **first lyricist **to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913, for his "profoundly sensitive, fresh, and lovely" poetry of Gitanjali. The Royal Asiatic Society elected him as a fellow.
 
• Tagore was dubbed "the Bard of Bengal" and went by the moniker** Gurudev, Kobiguru, and Biswakobi**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Devaki Nandan Khatri** was an Indian novelist who lived in Varanasi and published Chandrakanta, a historical fiction fantasy novel.
 
• **Harivansh Rai Bachchan** was an early twentieth-century Hindi poet and writer associated with the Nayi Kavita literary movement.
 
• **Ganga Da**s was a respected Udasi saint and a Hindi poet from Uttar Pradesh's Hapur area.

questions.question: Which department of the Government of India declares the minimum support prices?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Department of Agriculture and Cooperation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Department of Agriculture and Co-operation, **Government of India, declares Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for 23 crops before their sowing seasons, based on the recommendations of the **Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices.**
 
• It recommends MSPs of 23 commodities, are following:
 
 
• 7 oilseeds including groundnut, rapeseed-mustard, soybean, sesamum, sunflower, safflower, and nigerseed.
 
• 7 kinds of cereal including paddy, wheat, maize, sorghum, pearl millet, barley, and ragi.
 
• 5 pulses including gram, tur, moong, urad, and lentil.
 
• 4 commercial crops include copra, sugarcane, cotton, and raw jute.
 
 
 
• Despite the COVID-19 pandemic, the Government of India's policies and decisions on farmers' welfare have resulted in minor improvements in food grain production and maintained agriculture growth.
 
• **The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)**, chaired by** Hon'ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi,** has approved an increase in the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for all specified Rabi crops for the **Rabi Marketing Season (RMS) 2022-23** on September 8, 2021, when the sowing season is in advance.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, **formerly the Ministry of Agriculture, is a division of the Indian government that is responsible for the design and implementation of agricultural rules and regulations.
 
• **The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) **oversees all aspects of the Central Government's equity investments, including disinvestment in Central Public Sector Undertakings.
 
• **The Department of Economic Affairs** is the Union Government's nodal department for formulating and monitoring the country's economic policies and programmes that affect domestic and international economic management.
 
• **The Ministry of Finance** oversees the Department of Expenditure.

questions.question: Electoral roll is commonly known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**voter's list**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **An electoral roll** is a list of people who have registered to vote in a given jurisdiction's elections.
 
• **The Election Commission of India **is a constitutional body that prepares and revises electoral rolls and registers all eligible voters on a regular basis.
 
• **The Electoral Roll, **which is officially named the Voters' List and is usually known as the **Voters' List, **is compiled considerably before the election and provided to everyone in a democratic election.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Party-list **proportional representation systems require electoral lists.
 
• The application of nomination and election procedures results in the creation of an electoral list.
 
• **A political party**, a general assembly, or a board meeting may elect or appoint a nominating committee to add, and if necessary, prioritise list candidates according to their preferences, depending on the kind of election.
 
• In a selection meeting, the committee's recommended list can be altered, with new applicants being added or existing candidates being moved or deleted from the list.

questions.question: Who among the following was the chief scientist of World Health Organization as of August 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. Soumya Swaminathan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In March 2019, Dr Soumya Swaminathan** was named the** first Chief Scientist of the World Health Organisation(WHO)**.
 
• She offers 30 years of clinical care and research experience and has worked to integrate knowledge into relevant programmes throughout her career.
 
• She is an Indian paediatrician and a globally recognised researcher on tuberculosis and HIV.
 
• **From 2015 to 2017, Dr Swaminathan **served as the Secretary to the Government of India for Health Research and the Director-General of the Indian Council of Medical Research.
 
• She was also the Coordinator of the **UNICEF/UNDP/World Bank/WHO Special Programme** for Tropical Diseases Research and Training in Geneva from 2009 to 2011.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__ **

 
• **Dr. Zsuzsanna Jakab**, a native of Hungary, was named Deputy Director-General in 2019 after serving as WHO Regional Director for Europe since 2010.
 
• **Dr. Samira Asma** is the Assistant Director-General for Data, Analytics, and Delivery for Impact, where she leads the organization's efforts to establish a results framework for accountability and to use timely, reliable, and actionable data to drive progress toward the Triple Billion targets and health-related Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
 
• **Dr. Naoko Yamamoto** was the Assistant Director-General for Universal Health Coverage and Health Systems at the World Health Organization until recently.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India was established on:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**26 January 1950**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India, which is located on Tilak Marg in New Delhi, was **established on January 26, 1950.**
 
• It took the place of** both the Federal Court of India and the Privy Council's Judicial Committee**, which were at the time the highest courts in India.
 
• However, the first hearings and inauguration were held on January 28, 1950, at 9:45 a.m., when the judges took their seats. As a result, the date of establishment is considered official.
 
• The Supreme Court of India is India's top court and the highest judicial authority.
 
• It is the highest-ranking constitutional court with judicial review authority.
 
• The Supreme Court of India, which has a maximum of 34 judges and vast powers in the form of original, appellate, and advisory jurisdictions, is led by the Chief Justice of India.
 
• As India's supreme constitutional court, it hears appeals mostly from high courts in various states of the Union, as well as other courts and tribunals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Supreme Court of India:**

 
 
• Current Chief Justice of India: Dhananjaya Y. Chandrachud
 
• Authorized by: Article 124 of the Constitution of India
 
• 
 Established: **1 October 1937**; (as Federal Court of India)
 
 
 

**LINK__**:https://main.sci.gov.in/history#:~:text=Supreme%20Court%20of%20India%20came,on%20Tilak%20Marg%2C%20New%20Delhi.

questions.question: Mahendragiri is one of the highest peak in the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Eastern Ghats__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahendragiri** is a **mountain in Odisha,** India, located in the Rayagada subdivision of the** Gajapati district**.
 
• It is one of the highest peak in the eastern ghats.
 
 
• Now The highest peak in the Eastern Ghats is Jindhagada Peak.
 
 
 
• It is located at an** elevation of 1,501 metres **in the** Eastern Ghats**. After Deomali in the Koraput district, this is Odisha's second highest mountain peak. 
 
• Because of the various medicinal plants and other species present here, Mahendragiri hill and its surrounding areas have been designated as a biodiversity hotspot.
 
• **The Mahendragiri Biosphere Reserve Committee, **which was formed in November 2011, conducted its final meeting in December, following which it published its final report, which recommended that a Biosphere Reserve be established in the Mahendragiri Hill Complex. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Eastern Ghats **run from Odisha to Andhra Pradesh to Tamil Nadu in the south, passing through Karnataka and Telangana.
 
• **The Satpura Range **begins in eastern Gujarat and runs east through Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh before terminating in Chhattisgarh.
 
• **The Himalayas,** often known as the Himalayas, are a mountain range in Asia that separates the Indian subcontinent's plains from the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• **The Western Ghats,** also known as the Sahyadri Mountain range, is a mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of the Indian peninsula for 1,600 kilometres, passing through the states of Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Which law explains about the tides due to the moon and the sun?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Law of gravitation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The gravitational attraction between two bodies **is directly proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of their distance, according to **Newton's law of universal gravitation.**
 
• As a result, the gravitational attraction between two things increases as their mass increases and their distance decreases.
 
• The main force that causes tides is gravity.** Sir Isaac Newton** explained in 1687 that ocean tides are caused by the sun and moon's gravitational force on the earth's oceans.
 
• The gravitational attractive force is what causes tidal forces. The distance between two objects is frequently more important than their masses when it comes to tidal pressures on Earth.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The angle of the reflected** ray is equal to the angle of the incident ray when reflected off a smooth surface with respect to the normal to the surface, which is a line perpendicular to the surface at the point of contact, according to **the law of reflection**.
 
• **Law of refraction: **At the point of incidence, the incident ray refracted ray, and normal to the interface of two media all lie on the same plane.
 
• **The law of inertia, **commonly known as Newton's first law, states that if a body is at rest or moving in a straight line at a constant speed, it will remain at rest or continue to move in a straight path at constant speed until it is acted with by a force.

questions.question: With which of the following sports/games is Rani Rampal associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hockey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question: In which year was the Jal Jeevan Mission launched in India? The mission aims at providing potable water through its scheme of functional household tap connections.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2019**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)** is the genesis of **the Rashtriya Jal Jeevan Kosh (RJJK)**, which is a flagship programme of the Government of India inaugurated by** the Hon'ble Prime Minister on August 15, 2019**.
 
• By 2024, it hopes to have 'Functional Household Tap Connections' (FHTC) installed in every rural household in the country.
 
• Approximately 19 crore rural households in the country will be provided with tap water as part of the effort.
 
• Since the commencement of the Jal Jeevan Mission, almost 5 crore rural families have been connected to running water (JJM).
 
• **The Rashtriya Jal Jeevan Kosh (RJJK) **is a registered public charitable trust established by the Ministry of Jal Shakti's Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation. 
 
• It was established to act as a collection point for philanthropic contributions and to enable such contributions for the establishment of safe drinking water supplies in villages.
 
• Tap water can also be provided at schools, anganwadi centres, tribal residential schools, health-and-wellness centres, and other locations.

questions.question: Rukmini Devi Arundale is a famous classical dancer of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rukmini Devi Arundale** was an Indian theosophist, **dancer and choreographer of Bharatanatyam, **an Indian classical dance form, and animal rights campaigner.
 
• She was the** first woman in Indian history to be elected to the Rajya Sabha**, the country's highest house of parliament.
 
• She was the most prominent revivalist of Bharatanatyam from** its original 'Sadhir' style, **which was popular among temple dancers, the Devadasis, and she also sought to restore old Indian arts and crafts.
 
• Rukmini Devi was named one of India Today's** "100 People Who Shaped India."**
 
• In 1956, she received the Padma Bhushan, and in 1967, she received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam** is a significant Hindu form of Indian classical dance.
 
• **The initial sources of Bharatanatyam **are regarded to be Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra and Nandikeshvara's Abhinaya Darpana (Mirror of Gesture) (an Indian classical dance form).
 
• The dance form is also briefly addressed in Someshwara III's Kannada work Manasollasa.
 
• Since ancient times, it has thrived in the temples and courts of southern India.
 
• It is one of eight well-known Indian classical dance genres that reflects South Indian religious themes and spiritual ideals, particularly those of Shaivism, Vaishnavism, and Shaktism, collectively known as Hinduism.

questions.question: An official enumeration of population done periodically is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**census**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A census** is a periodic** official enumeration of the population**.
 
• **The first census in India** was conducted in 1872. However, the first complete census was done in 1881.
 
• Since then, every ten years, censuses have been held. The most thorough source of demographic, social, and economic statistics is the Indian Census.
 
• The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, conducts a census every ten years.
 
• In 2021, India will conduct its 16th census.
 
• **Union Home Minister Amit Shah **announced in September 2019 that the 2021 national census would be conducted entirely digitally via a mobile phone application. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Any statistical component that influences population growth or decline can be included in** demographics**, although six characteristics are particularly important: **population size, density, age structure, fecundity (birth rates), mortality (death rates), and sex ratio (Dodge 2006). **
 
• **The Citizenship Act of 1955 **was amended in 2003, requiring the development of the **National Register of Citizens (NRC)**. Its goal is to identify and expel illegal immigrants by documenting all legal citizens of India.
 
• **The National Population Register (NPR)** is a database of people who live in a hamlet, rural region, town, ward, or delimited area within a ward in a city or town.

questions.question: Who is the chairperson of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Vice-President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Vice-President of India** is the **chairperson of the Rajya Sabha**.
 
• **Muppavarapu Venkaiah Naidu **is an Indian politician who has been serving as India's vice president since 2017.
 
• He formerly served in the Modi Cabinet as the minister of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation, Urban Development, and Information and Broadcasting.
 
• He was a senior member of the Bharatiya Janata Party and the party's national president from 2002 to 2004.
 
• He formerly served in the Atal Bihari Vajpayee cabinet as the Union Cabinet Minister for Rural Development.
 
• On August 11, 2017, he was sworn in as** the Vice President of India and Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.**
 
• He earned 516 votes, compared to 244 for UPA candidate **Gopalkrishna Gandhi.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The vice president of India** is the** deputy to the president of India**, who is the head of state of the Republic of India.
 
• After the president, the vice president is the second-highest constitutional office, ranking second in order of precedence and first in line of succession to the presidency.
 
• The vice president determines whether a bill is a money bill or not when it is introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• He will send a measure filed in the Rajya Sabha to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha if he believes it is a money bill.

questions.question: Which state among the following is the largest producer of coffee?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Karnataka** is the **largest producer of coffee**.
 
• With **203,445 MT** of coffee output in 2019-20, the state produced over** 70% of India's total coffee production**.
 
• Karnataka's major coffee variety is Robusta, however, the state also produces a limited amount of Arabica.
 
• The state has ideal climatic conditions for coffee plantations, including high altitude, sloppy mountains, and adequate rainfall.
 
• The coffee plantation is located in the Karnataka districts of Chikkamagaluru, Hassan, and Kodagu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Coffee cultivation** in India dates back to the 16th-century Sufi mystic Baba Budan, who returned from Yemen with "seven seeds" of "Mocha" coffee beans and planted them on "Baba Budan Giris" in Karnataka.
 
• Coffee plantations gradually spread over south India, and commercial coffee plantations began in the 18th century.
 
• Coffee is grown mostly in the southern Indian states of **Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• It is also grown in India's northeastern states.
